title: 1964 AHSME Problem 13
statement: A circle is inscribed in a triangle with side lengths \(8,\) \(13,\) and \(17.\) Let the segments of the side of length \(8,\) made by a point of tangency, be \(r\) and \(s,\) with \(r\lt s.\) What is the ratio \(r:s?\)

solutions.text:
The semiperimeter is \(\frac{8+13+17}{2}=19.\) At the endpoints of the side of length \(8,\) the tangent lengths are \(19-13=6\) and \(19-17=2.\) Thus \(r:s=2:6=1:3.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is A.
hints: Compute the semiperimeter of the triangle
A tangency segment adjacent to a vertex equals the semiperimeter minus the opposite side
